3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: It was a Saturday afternoon, my first break from work in what felt like years, and the weather couldn't have been more perfect. Trying to keep my mind off the upheaval sparked by the Circas assassination, I lit the backyard grill.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: Monica and Deana were out shopping for craft supplies, and I'd given the staff the day off. It was just myself and Franc at home.
4.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Media_SordlandToday_Bias"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Media_SordlandToday_Bias"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_EconomicRelief_DontEnactPlan"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_EconomicRelief_DontEnactPlan"] == true) == false)

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: Sure enough, as soon as Franc glimpsed the grill and the meat, he stepped outside to join me.

6.speaker: Franc
6.text: "Don't get any ideas, Dad. I'm only here for the ribs."

7.speaker: Player
7.text: “And that, my boy, is how bribery works.”

8.speaker: Franc
8.text: “Ha. What a great example you're setting.”

9.speaker: Player
9.text: “Well, you're going to have to work for them. Help me fan these flames.”

10.speaker: Player
10.text: “Children who talk back to their fathers don't get dinner. Fan these flames, will you?”

11.speaker: Narrator
11.text: Franc sighed and waved the fan lazily, almost causing the fire to die out.

12.speaker: Player
12.text: “You keep it up at that rate and we'll never have dinner. Put your back into it!”

13.speaker: Player
13.text: "Never mind, I'll do it myself. Just bring the large serving platter from the kitchen.”

14.speaker: Player
14.text: "It worked, didn't it? Everyone has their price. Remember that."

15.speaker: Player
15.text: “It's politics, Franc. You're old enough to learn the ways of the world.'

16.speaker: Narrator
16.text: He looked like he was going to say something, but quickly closed his mouth and nodded.

19.speaker: Narrator
19.text: He continued just as listlessly as before.

20.speaker: Franc
20.text: “Oh, I'm one of your employees now?”

21.speaker: Player_Italic
21.text: Show him how to do it properly.

23.speaker: Player
23.text: “My father would have slapped me for this.”

25.speaker: Franc
25.text: “I guess I should be grateful that you don't...”

27.speaker: Player
27.text: “Don't make me angry. Do as I say.”

28.speaker: Player
28.text: “Can't I even request something from my son now?”

30.speaker: Narrator
30.text: Franc returned with a tray large enough to hold all the meat and vegetables. The fire was still burning weakly.

32.speaker: Narrator
32.text: He grabbed the fan and started quickly waving it over the coals. The fire roared to life.

35.speaker: Narrator
35.text: He turned to look at me with a grin on his face, as if he was expecting praise.

37.speaker: Franc
37.text: “Thank you, sir. It is in our utmost interest to fulfill our duties with precision. The grilling shall commence in exactly 1 minute and 32 seconds."

38.speaker: Narrator
38.text: That was a spot-on impersonation of Lucian. We looked at each other for a second, then burst out laughing.

40.speaker: Narrator
40.text: It was rare for Franc to agree with anything I said nowadays. I turmed to tend to the fire.

41.speaker: Narrator
41.text: I realized my throat was parched. There was a six-pack of beer in the kitchen.

42.speaker: Player
42.text: "Franc, can you get me a beer?"

43.speaker: Player
43.text: "Why don't you bring us a couple of beers?"

44.speaker: Narrator
44.text: He looked at me in disbelief.

45.speaker: Player_Italic
45.text: Get up and grab a beer.

46.speaker: Narrator
46.text: Franc got up without saying anything, went to the kitchen and returned with a cold beer.

49.speaker: Franc
49.text: "You mean, I can--? But Mom told me--"

50.speaker: Narrator
50.text: He stopped himself, quickly ran inside and returned with two beers. We cracked them open, clinked the bottles and gazed out at the city skyline.

51.speaker: Narrator
51.text: I opened the beer and gazed out at the city skyline. Father and son, we enjoyed the silence together.

52.speaker: Narrator
52.text: I opened it, sat down, and gazed out at the city skyline with my son.

53.speaker: Narrator
53.text: For a moment, my thoughts flashed back to my childhood and my relationship with my own father.

61.speaker: Narrator
61.text: My father was a poor man who struggled to provide for us on his meager income. He put me to work on the farm long before I was Franc's age, and even then, we couldn't always make ends meet. Yet, we were always close as a family.

62.speaker: Narrator
62.text: My father was a rich man. We never had to worry about food, clothes, or anything else. Yet he was nearly always away -- and constantly distracted on the rare occasions when he was at home.

63.speaker: Narrator
63.text: My father was a hard-working man and always had our best interests in mind -- or at least, that's what he always said. But he had a temper, and would lash out at my mother in fights I could hear from my bedroom. By the time I was Franc's age, we seldom spoke.

64.speaker: Narrator
64.text: Now that I was the president, I knew Franc would never face the same hardships I had. I couldn't deny that I felt a bit jealous.

65.speaker: Narrator
65.text: Now that I was the president, I was worried that I would end up just like my father. Distant and absent from Franc's life.

66.speaker: Narrator
66.text: Now that I was the president, I was facing more stress than my father ever had. I would have to work hard not to take my frustrations out on my family.

68.speaker: Player
68.text: “We are family. You can ask anything.”

70.speaker: Franc
70.text: “It's just... I feel like there's so much you've been hiding from me. About your past, and about what's going on right now.”

71.speaker: Franc
71.text: “But... what was it like, back then? Uncle Petr said the two of you went through a lot..."

72.speaker: Franc
72.text: “I'm not a kid anymore. You can tell me."

73.speaker: Narrator
73.text: Before I could gather my thoughts, the familiar images started flashing before my eyes.

74.speaker: Narrator
74.text: Images of soldiers advancing towards me and my friends, weapons drawn. Of people I knew -- friends and neighbors -- being dragged through streets and murdered in alleyways.

76.speaker: Player
76.text: “I don't want to talk about it.”

78.speaker: Narrator
78.text: Hearing the faint trembling in my voice, Franc understood and pushed no further.

80.speaker: Player
80.text: “But you're nearly a grown man. Let's talk about it.”

82.speaker: Franc
82.text: “It's okay. I'm sorry. I shouldn't have asked you about it.”

83.speaker: Player
83.text: "I was barely older than you are now..."

90.speaker: Player
90.text: "I was barely older than you are now..."

92.speaker: Player_Italic
92.text: Tell Franc about the coup of 1927.

93.speaker: Player_Italic
93.text: Tell Franc about the civil war.

94.speaker: Player
94.text: “Actually, never mind. Now is not the time to talk about the past.”

96.speaker: Player
96.text: "The same soldiers that were supposed to protect Sordland's citizens pointed their guns at us..."

100.speaker: Narrator
100.text: I stopped there and turned my head away from Franc.

102.speaker: Player
102.text: "It was right after I met your mother..."

127.text: "It was right after I met your mother..."

131.text: "It was right after I met your mother..."

132.speaker: Player_Italic
132.text: Tell Franc about the clash between Luderin and Rikard.

145.speaker: Franc
145.text: “I know I don't understand how easy my life is sometimes.”

146.speaker: Narrator
146.text: Franc hesitated, then moved over to where I was sitting and gave me an awkward pat on the back.

147.speaker: Franc
147.text: "I know I complain sometimes, but my problems are nothing compared to what you went through."

149.speaker: Narrator
149.text: Before Franc could say anything else, I heard the front door unlock. Deana and Monica's voices and the sounds of rustling shopping bags filled the house.

150.speaker: Franc
150.text: “I should get some studying done before dinner. But thanks for this, Dad. I mean it.”

151.speaker: Narrator
151.text: Franc went in and dashed upstairs.

152.speaker: Narrator
152.text: I took a long sip from my beer, looking at the city and the now-setting sun.

153.speaker: Narrator
153.text: I hoped that talking to Franc about my past had been the right decision. Part of me felt as if some sort of burden had been lifted.

157.speaker: Narrator
157.text: But I had the same nightmares again that night.

158.speaker: Narrator
158.text: But I had the same nightmares again that night.

160.speaker: Narrator
160.text: Franc leaned forward in his chair, his eyes wide.

161.speaker: Player_Italic
161.text: Tell him about the soldiers beating you.

162.speaker: Player_Italic
162.text: Refrain from telling him the brutality.

163.speaker: Player_Italic
163.text: Tell him that you ran for your life like a coward.

164.speaker: Player_Italic
164.text: Refrain from telling him about your quick escape.

166.speaker: Player
166.text: "I still feel my flight was justified -- anyone would do the same..."

167.speaker: Narrator
167.text: I stopped there and turned my head away from Franc.

172.speaker: Player_Italic
172.text: Refrain from telling him about the girl.

173.speaker: Narrator
173.text: I trailed off. There were some things my son didn't have to know.

174.speaker: Narrator
174.text: Franc leaned back in his chair. His shoulders slumped heavily.

175.speaker: Narrator
175.text: Franc leaned back in his chair. His shoulders slumped heavily.

176.speaker: Narrator
176.text: Franc's face had grown pale. He turned his eyes away from me.

181.speaker: Player_Italic
181.text: Refrain from telling him about your escape.

182.speaker: Player_Italic
182.text: Tell him that you ran away.

183.speaker: Narrator
183.text: I trailed off, hoping Franc wouldn't ask for any more details.

184.speaker: Narrator
184.text: Years later, I still felt that I was right. How could mere civilians go against a fully trained army, regardless of how just their cause was?

185.speaker: Narrator
185.text: Franc turned away, lost in his own thoughts.

186.speaker: Narrator
186.text: Franc shifted in his seat, visibly uncomfortable.

187.speaker: Narrator
187.text: Sure enough, as soon as Franc glimpsed the grill and the meat, he stepped outside to join me.

191.speaker: Franc
191.text: “Dad, is there going to be a civil war in Sordland?”

193.speaker: Player
193.text: “No. I will never let that happen.”

194.speaker: Player_Italic
194.text: Say nothing and avoid his question.

204.speaker: Player
204.text: “I didn't say bribery was good, did I? You can always make the moral choice and turn these delicious ribs down...”

205.speaker: Narrator
205.text: Franc smiled for a second. I turned to tend to the fire.

208.speaker: Franc
208.text: “Geez, you're barely ever here, and when you are you order me around like I'm the butler?”

209.speaker: Franc
209.text: “As long as it's a request, not an order.”

213.speaker: Player
213.text: “Franc! I said don't make me angry!”

214.speaker: Franc
214.text: “Stop yelling at me. Why are you always like this?"

215.speaker: Player
215.text: “I'm sorry. Work is overwhelming sometimes. I shouldn't have taken it out on you.”

216.speaker: Franc
216.text: “Yeah, sure, it's okay. You know, being the president's son isn't exactly a picnic either."

217.speaker: Player
217.text: “I can only imagine. I'm proud of how well you've been handling everything.”

218.speaker: Player
218.text: “We can talk about it more later. For now, will you please go fetch the tray so we can eat?”

221.speaker: Player
221.text: “No. You're my son and I'm asking you. Can you bring the tray now, please?”

224.speaker: Player
224.text: “Damn your generation. You are all the same. Weak.”

225.speaker: Franc
225.text: "Weak?! Dad, can't you see you're not the only one having a hard time here?"

226.speaker: Franc
226.text: "You never even asked me how it feels -- being treated differently in school, everyone asking me about the riots all the time, not even being able to take a piss without those guards following me..."

227.speaker: Player
227.text: “Oh, cry me a river. Grow a spine and make something of yourself.”

228.speaker: Franc
228.text: “I'm sorry for being spineless, okay? Are you happy now? I'll get your goddamn tray."

229.speaker: Narrator
229.text: Franc returned with a tray large enough to hold all the meat and vegetables. He shoved it at me.

232.speaker: Narrator
232.text: He ran inside the house before I could say anything. The door slammed behind him.

233.speaker: Narrator
233.text: I took a long sip from my beer.

234.speaker: Player
234.text: “I've warned you. Shut up and do as I say -- or else.”

236.speaker: Franc
236.text: “Or else what? You're going to slap me? Beat me?”

237.speaker: Franc
237.text: “Fine. I'll go get your goddamn tray."

253.speaker: Franc
253.text: “You will have to go through my secretary first.”

254.speaker: Narrator
254.text: He laughed and started making his way to the kitchen.

258.speaker: Franc
258.text: “One more thing, though -- I know you joined the Young Sords back then. Do you mind if I ask why?”

265.speaker: Franc
265.text: “One more thing, though -- I know that you joined Red Youth back then. Do you mind if I ask why?”
265.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Relations_Franc_Opinion"] <= -5) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_University_Political_Nationalist"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_University_Political_Socialist"] == true)

266.speaker: Franc
266.text: “One more thing, though -- I know that you managed to not take any sides. Do you mind if I ask why?”
266.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Relations_Franc_Opinion"] <= -5) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_University_Political_Nationalist"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_University_Political_Socialist"] == true) == false)

267.speaker: Player
267.text: “Yes, I do mind. I don't want to talk about it.”

268.speaker: Player
268.text: “Sordland was under attack by communists and I had to defend the country.”

269.speaker: Franc
269.text: “Okay. I was just curious, that's all.”

270.speaker: Narrator
270.text: Franc raised his eyebrows, his curiosity still not satisfied. But sensing my reluctance to go on, he simply nodded.

271.speaker: Player
271.text: “I had to survive somehow in that environment and I made a choice.”

272.speaker: Player
272.text: “Yes, I do mind. I don't want to talk about it.”

273.speaker: Franc
273.text: “Okay. I was just curious, that's all.”

274.speaker: Player
274.text: “A communist revolution for Sordland was and still is the only way.”

275.speaker: Narrator

276.speaker: Player
276.text: “I had to survive somehow in that environment, and I made a choice.”

277.speaker: Player
277.text: “Yes, I do mind. I don't want to talk about it.”

278.speaker: Franc
278.text: “Okay. I was just curious, that's all.”

279.speaker: Narrator
279.text: Franc raised his eyebrows, his curiosity still not satisfied. But sensing my reluctance to go on, he simply nodded.

280.speaker: Player
280.text: “I didn't want to be part of the violence."

281.speaker: Player
281.text: “They are two sides of the same coin.”

283.speaker: Player
283.text: “Don't act like you've done something special, Franc.”

284.speaker: Narrator
284.text: He gave me a blank stare and then turned his eyes away.

307.speaker: Narrator
307.text: I wasn't sure how he felt about me at the moment. But I did know how he felt about barbecued ribs. Our cook had left some marinating in the refrigerator.

311.speaker: Player
311.text: "So, you've finally decided to speak to me again?"

312.speaker: Player
312.text: "Well, look who's finally out of his room."

313.speaker: Player
313.text: "Come to spend some quality time with your old man, have you?"

317.speaker: Franc
317.text: "You should talk, Dad. I never see you at home anymore."

318.speaker: Franc
318.text: "Sure, if you can spare a few minutes out of your busy schedule."

322.speaker: Player
322.text: "I'm sorry, I know I haven't been around very often lately. But I'm happy to see you now."

323.speaker: Player
323.text: "Look, son, I'm preoccupied with matters of national importance."

324.speaker: Franc
324.text: "Yes, Mr. President. Whatever you say, Mr. President."

326.speaker: Player
326.text: "But right now, nothing's more important than these ribs."

328.speaker: Franc
328.text: "It's okay. I know you've got the most stressful job in the country. And you've got to feed your family on top of it all...”

329.speaker: Narrator
329.text: We both chuckled. I turned to tend to the fire.

330.speaker: Franc
330.text: "Like at dinner that night after the ball. You told me everything was under control, but it wasn't, was it?"

334.speaker: Franc
334.text: "I know what happened in the '20s -- we learned all about it in school. Now, with the protests and the riots, is it going to be the same thing?"

335.speaker: Franc
335.text: "Like at dinner that night after the ball. Maybe I shouldn't have brought it up in front of Deana, but I was right, wasn't I? It's bad."

339.speaker: Narrator
339.text: The shock and grief on the faces of fathers, mothers and orphaned children.

347.text: "I was barely older than you are now..."

348.speaker: Narrator
348.text: Franc kept listening, a shocked look on his face.

349.speaker: Player
349.text: "I'm here to listen to them, no matter what they are."

350.speaker: Player
350.text: "You're damn right. Your generation will never understand."
